title: Oncall Triage & Communication Canvas
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Summary

This runbook describes a structured canvas for oncall triage, incident communication, and rapid containment for inference workloads. It focuses on: SLO and error-budget-aware decisions, capacity and routing checks, stakeholder communication templates, evidence packaging for post-incident review, and short playbooks to move from alert to recovery. The document is intended for SREs, oncall engineers, incident commanders, and on-call responders for Redwood Inference.

Goals

- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-ack by standardizing triage checkpoints.
- Make burn-rate-driven decisions deterministic (when to pause low-priority tenants, when to enable burst pools).
- Provide clear, reusable communication artifacts for internal and customer-facing updates.
- Ensure evidence collected is sufficient for RCA and SLO impact assessment.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to model serving, routing, and capacity-related incidents (including quantized-serving latency regressions, OOM cascades, KV cache corruption, and burst overloads).
- Assumes access to: Redwood Console (model telemetry), Grafana dashboards, PagerDuty, Slack (#incidents, #sre-war-room), and the evidence-store (S3 bucket with access audit).

Key roles and responsibilities

1) PagerDuty responder (first ACK): triage initial signal, run steps 1–4 in the triage checklist.
2) Incident Commander (IC): coordinates comms, decides severity, invokes runbook actions (routing, throttling, tenant isolation).
3) Service Owner / Model Steward: provides model-specific context (expected latency profile, recent rollouts).
4) Communications lead: prepares status updates and customer notices if needed.
5) Evidence steward: packages traces, sample tokens, and Grafana snapshots for postmortem.

SLO and error-budget decision ladder

- Baseline SLOs:
  - Latency p95 <= 120 ms for hosted text-generation endpoints.
  - Availability >= 99.9% (monthly).
  - Embedding throughput p90 >= X (normalized to 1k tokens/s per shard).

- Error budget burn thresholds (for a single service tenant-aggregated view):
  1. Normal (< 10% burn in 24h): standard triage, monitor.
  2. Elevated (10%–50% burn in 24h): notify Product, enable higher-fidelity tracing on affected routes, prepare to throttle low-priority tenants.
  3. Critical (> 50% burn in 24h OR predicted to exhaust within 6h): IC declares Severity 1/2 depending on customer impact; take protective measures (evict non-op staff traffic, warm up dedicated pools, enable canary rollback).

NOTE: Burn calculations are tenant-weighted by committed capacity for Dedicated customers; hosted customers are weighted by usage. Use the error-budget API endpoint: curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/errorbudgets?tenant=$TENANT-ID

Triage checklist (first 12 minutes)

1) Acknowledge and classify
   - Acknowledge PagerDuty alert within 2 minutes.
   - Classify: latency | error rate | OOM | memory leak | cold-start regressions | routing/fallbacks.
2) Quick impact sweep (2–6 minutes)
   - Check Grafana: p50/p95/p99 latency panels for the affected model and aggregate.
   - Query request rate and queue depth on the serving tier (example PromQL):
     sum(rate(requests_total{service=\"runtime\",model=~\".*\"}[1m])) by (model)
   - Verify whether KV cache hit ratio dropped: kv_cache_hits / kv_cache_requests.
3) Hit isolation knobs (6–10 minutes)
   - If queue depth > 3x baseline AND latency p95 increased > 2x, apply tenant throttles per the throttling matrix below.
   - If OOMs observed on quantized pods: enable mem-slim mode (routing flag) and remove larger batch sizes from the router.
4) Evidence snapshot and initial comms (10–12 minutes)
   - Post to #incidents: short summary (one-line), impact, IC, next update cadence. Use template below.
   - Save Grafana snapshots and a representative 1-minute packet capture from the router.

Throttling matrix (safe defaults)

| Condition | Immediate action | Owner | Rollback condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Queue depth > 3x + p95 > 2x | Apply tenant soft-throttle: 70% of baseline rate | IC / runtime-ops | p95 < 1.2x and queue depth < 1.5x |
| Error rate spike > 5% absolute | Route to fallback model variant (lower-cost, higher-stability) | Model Steward | error rate < 1% for 10m |
| Memory reclaim loop / repeated OOMs | Evict speculative batchers and pin to lower-batch profile | SRE | no OOMs for 30m and memory pressure normalizes |

Routing and fallback steps

- When activating fallback routes:
  1. Update routing policy in the router service: routerctl set-policy --route <route> --policy fallback-variant.
  2. Validate via canary: send 50 synthetic requests using the canary harness.
  3. If canary success (error rate delta < 0.5% and latency delta < +20ms), promote the fallback and increase traffic in 10% increments every 5 minutes.

Communication templates

- Initial incident post (Slack #incidents):
  [INCIDENT] <short-id> — <one-line summary>
  Impact: <services/customers affected>
  IC: <name> | Severity: <S1/S2/S3>
  Next update: <ETA in minutes>

- External customer facing (email / support):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Service disruption affecting <feature>
  Body: We are investigating increased latency for <model/service>. Our engineering team has identified the impact and is actively mitigating. Current ETA for next update: <time>. We will follow up with root cause and customer impact in the post-incident summary.

Evidence checklist for post-incident review

- Required evidence items (submit to evidence-store under incidents/<short-id>/):
  - Grafana snapshots (latency, error-rate, queue-depth) covering 30 minutes before to 30 minutes after alert.
  - Router request logs (sampled) for affected models (include token-level IDs, not raw customer data).
  - A 10-second heap/profile dump if memory issues suspected.
  - Error traces from Sentry with tags for model and route.
  - Error budget delta export (CSV) for the affected tenants.
  - Command history (kubectl/routerctl/ops scripts) used during mitigation.

Post-incident review (quick template)

- Timeline: concisely list timestamps for detection, ack, mitigation, resolution, customer communication.
- Impact summary: affected customers, SLOs impacted, total error-budget consumed.
- Root-cause hypothesis and supporting evidence.
- Corrective actions and owners (tag owner_team and due date).
- Severity classification sanity check and whether escalation was correct.
- Lessons learned: what to automate next, dashboard/pager adjustments.

Automations and tooling guidance

- Use the incident generator to rehearse: python tools/incident_replay.py --scenario latency_spike --duration 10m --tenant sample-tenant.
- For evidence capture, rely on the runbook helper: runbook-helper capture --incident <id> --folders grafana,routerlogs,sentry --compress. The helper will return a signed URL for the evidence bundle.
- Alert tuning guidance: prefer two-stage alerts (warning then critical) with the following thresholds:
  - Latency-warning: p95 > 90ms sustained for 5m.
  - Latency-critical: p95 > 200ms for 3m OR p99 > 500ms for 1m.

Capacity playbook shortcuts (when capacity is the suspected cause)

1) Check headroom in dedicated pools: HEADROOM = provisioned_capacity - in_use_capacity. If HEADROOM < 15% for > 10m, trigger dedicated-reserve flow.
2) Rapid warm pool: instruct capacity-orchestrator to spin up n+2 shards for the affected model: capacityctl warm --model <id> --count 2.
3) Redistribute traffic: enable regional routing preference to unaffected region if latency and egress rules permit.

Oncall drills and checklists (weekly cadence)

- Weekly micro-drill: 30-minute scenario run using incident_replay. Rotate IC role among SREs.
- Monthly table-top: review latest three incidents, validate evidence bundles and action item closure.

Runbook change control

- Any change to throttling matrix, error-budget ladder, or alert thresholds requires:
  1. Draft PR in docs repo with changes.
  2. Two reviewer approvals from eng-sre.
  3. One rehearsal in staging using incident_replay.

Appendices

A) Quick CLI snippets
- Fetch error budget for tenant:
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/errorbudgets?tenant=$TENANT-ID | jq
- Snapshot Grafana panel (example):
  grafana-cli snapshots create --panel-id 42 --from \"now-30m\" --to \"now\" --org 1
- Trigger soft throttle:
  routerctl throttle --tenant $TENANT-ID --rate 0.7

B) Evidence file naming convention
- incidents/<short-id>/grafana-<panel>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.png
- incidents/<short-id>/routerlogs-sample-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.ndjson
- incidents/<short-id>/heapdump-<pod>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.tar.gz

C) Escalation contact matrix

| Severity | PagerDuty | Escalate to | Customer comms owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | paging-sre | Eng Director oncall, CTO | Head of Customer Success |
| S2 | paging-sre | Eng Manager oncall, Product TPM | Support Ops Lead |
| S3 | email | Service Owner | Support Team |

D) Change history
- 2025-04-10: Initial published by Asha Kapoor.
- 2025-10-02: Added throttle matrix and error-budget ladder; reviewer: Miguel Torres.
- 2026-01-15: Added capacity shortcuts and evidence helper CLI; reviewer: Priya Nair.

If you are oncall and this playbook is used to resolve an incident, file a short blameless retro within 72 hours and attach the evidence bundle link to the post-incident review page.

End of document.
